title: Isaiah 47
paragraphs: ¹ 'Come down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter Babylon; sit on the ground, for your throne is gone, daughter of the Chaldeans. No longer will you be called tender and delicate. ² Take up the millstones and grind the grain; remove your veil. Strip off your skirt, bare your legs, and wade through the streams. ³ Your nakedness will be exposed; your shame will be seen. I will take vengeance; I will spare no one.' ⁴ Our Redeemer — the LORD of Armies is his name — is the Holy One of Israel. ⁵ 'Sit in silence, go into darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans; no longer will you be called queen of the kingdoms.'

⁶ 'I was angry with my people and desecrated my inheritance; I gave them into your hand, and you showed them no mercy. Even on the elderly you laid a very heavy yoke. ⁷ You said, I will be queen forever! But you did not consider these things or reflect on what might happen. ⁸ Now then, listen, you lover of pleasure, you who live in complacency, who says in your heart, I am, and there is no one besides me. I will never be a widow or suffer the loss of children. ⁹ Both of these will overtake you in a moment, on a single day: loss of children and widowhood. They will come upon you in full measure, in spite of your many sorceries and all your powerful enchantments. ¹⁰ You felt secure in your wickedness and said, No one sees me. Your wisdom and knowledge have led you astray, and you have said in your heart, I am, and there is no one besides me.'

¹¹ 'Disaster will come upon you, and you will not know how to ward it off. Calamity will fall on you, and you will not be able to avert it; ruin will overwhelm you suddenly, before you know it. ¹² Keep on, then, with your magic spells and with the many sorceries you have practiced since childhood. Perhaps you will succeed, perhaps you will inspire terror. ¹³ All the advice you have received has only worn you out. Let your astrologers come forward, those stargazers who make predictions month by month — let them save you from what is coming. ¹⁴ See, they are like straw; the fire will burn them up. They cannot even save themselves from the power of the flame. These are not coals for warmth; this is not a fire to sit by. ¹⁵ That is all they can do for you — these advisors you have wearied yourself with, who have dealt with you since your childhood. Each one goes off in his own direction; none can save you.'
